hints.content: The arrow points to all values less than $4$.
So, the inequality represents everything **less than $4$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**



[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 4. A line running to the left starts at 4 and continues.

choices.clue:
The graph of $ 4<x$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 4. A line running to the right starts at 4 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/6ed304117041490280f64ddf2b4439d6c97140e4)

The graph of $ 3>x$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 3. A line running to the left starts at 3 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/f1ee77d6fdf6f0072094f6bf2bfede80bc92a862)

The graph of $ 3<x$ actually looks like this:


![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 3. A line running to the right starts at 3 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/956a58a8e2d50ba79ccdfca4b39e6d7b58ffc011)
